_note: Labelled pairs for `ctx patterns --check-meaning`: does the embedding model keep look-alikes apart (same: false) and group the same problem told with other words (same: true)? Pairs marked stopped_by_place share only a model: meaning is never compared for them (it needs the same element or an overlapping scope), so they are shown but not counted. The others pass place and guards, so only meaning decides. Calibrated on gemini-embedding-001 on 2026-11-07: same >= 0.802, counted look-alikes <= 0.691, threshold 0.78. See docs/patterns.md.

pairs.why: breaker F3: real LLM wording vs label

a.summary: When RAD-254 at the Turku harbour hut is completely dead, breaker F3 has usually tripped; reset it and empty the dehumidifier tray before replacing the radio.
a.action: Reset breaker F3 in the cabinet left of the door and empty the dehumidifier tray; check that the radio comes back before replacing it.
a.diagnosis: the dehumidifier trips breaker F3 in heavy sea fog

b.summary: When RAD-254 is dead at Turku harbour hut due to dehumidifier tripping breaker F3 in sea fog, flip breaker F3 back up and empty the dehumidifier tray rather than replacing the radio unit.
b.action: Flip F3 back up in the grey breaker cabinet left of the door and empty the dehumidifier tray.
b.diagnosis: The dehumidifier trips breaker F3 in the grey cabinet left of the door when sea fog is bad or when the tray is full.

pairs.why: SFP forwarding state: real LLM wording vs label

a.summary: On older transmission units, after an SFP swap, UP + normal optics + zero counters means a forwarding-state issue: bounce the interface before replacing hardware or rebooting.
a.action: Disable the interface, wait a little, then enable it again.
a.diagnosis: forwarding-state issue, not a faulty SFP

b.summary: Bounce interface (disable, wait, enable) after SFP swap when link is UP, optical levels normal, but traffic counters sit at zero
b.action: Bounce the interface: disable, wait a bit, then enable
b.diagnosis: No traffic after SFP swap despite link being UP and RX power normal

pairs.why: evening sync loss told with other words

a.action: Reset the timing port; sync comes back within a minute or two.

b.summary: The node loses its clock reference around nine in the evening; links stay green but nothing passes.
b.action: Re-initialise the PTP interface; timing lock returns after a minute or two.

a.action: Wait about 8 to 10 minutes after a power cycle before checking the management port.
a.diagnosis: management port is slow to come up after a cold start, the unit is not stuck

pairs.why: same radio: cold morning link flap vs antenna profile lost on restart

a.summary: On very cold mornings RAD-198 flaps until about 10:00 and recovers by itself; do not dispatch a crew before then.
a.action: Do not dispatch a crew; wait until about 10:00 and dispatch only if the link is still flapping.
a.diagnosis: ice on the dish that melts once the sun reaches it

b.summary: After a restart RAD-198 (RU-200, firmware 2.3) comes up on the factory profile; reload 'Profile 1' from the front panel menu or the link stays degraded.
b.action: After the restart, open the front panel menu and choose 'Load profile 1'.
b.diagnosis: the restart resets the antenna profile on firmware 2.3

pairs.why: same model only (RU-200): RAD-176 frost margin ('on RAD-176 only') vs RAD-198 iced dish; found by the first real run (0.823)

a.summary: On RAD-176 only (RU-200, Ounasvaara, antenna in the shade of the cliff) the link margin dips on hard frost mornings (below -25 C) and recovers by itself in about 20 minutes once the heater has warmed the unit; do not realign the antenna. Other RU-200s are not affected.
a.action: Wait about 20 minutes and re-check the link margin.
a.diagnosis: cold unit, margin recovers after the heater warms it
